newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures mostly end up on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures mostly end up on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended higher Tuesday in moderate trade, with front months lifted by technical buying and short covering when downside momentum stalled shortly after the open.
January climbed 17.4 cents to close at $3.396 per million British thermal units. February settled 11.8 cents higher at $3.13. Most other deferreds ended steady to up by 6.8 cents.

"It was mostly technicals today. It's pretty mild everywhere, but it's not going to stay mild all winter. The weather will change," said one Texas-based trader, noting short covering helped buoy front months.

Despite weakness in the cash today on forecasts for milder Midwest and Eastern temperatures this week, traders said it was too soon to write off winter, particularly with stocks still low, and many expected more volatility in both directions depending on the weather.

Now that the $3.44-46 January gap was filled on ACCESS Tuesday, technical traders pegged resistance in the $3.50 area, then at $3.70 and then at the contract high of $3.80. Support was seen at $3.19, then $3.11 and then at $3.04.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped Tuesday by 10 cents to about the $3.20 level. Midcon pipes were down five to 10 cents to the $3.15-20 area.
The 12-month strip gained five cents to $2.474. NYMEX said 36,510 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 38,923.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas finished six cents higher at $1.63, while deferreds settled steady to down one cent. NYMEX said 12 Alberta contracts traded versus eight on Monday.
NYMEX Permian natgas again was untraded, but January settled up 10 cents at $3.05.

On the KCBT, January ended 16 cents higher at $3.255, while deferreds closed up by 2.5 to 12 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.4 cents to 14.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 162 lots traded, down from Monday's 388.
